summary: Tambillos Airport (COW) is a small airfield serving the Coquimbo area along Chile's Pacific coast. It primarily handles general aviation and private flights rather than scheduled commercial service. The airport sits in a semi-arid coastal landscape characteristic of the Coquimbo Region, providing convenient access to nearby communities and coastal attractions.
faqs:
Q: Does Tambillos Airport offer commercial passenger flights?
A: No, it is classified as a small airport and primarily serves general aviation, private aircraft, and occasional charter operations.

Q: Where is Tambillos Airport located relative to the city of Coquimbo?
A: It is situated south of the Coquimbo-La Serena metropolitan area, in a rural stretch of the coastal region.

Q: What kind of facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small airfield, it offers basic aviation infrastructure with limited passenger amenities, typical of regional general aviation strips.

Q: Can I fly into Coquimbo on a major airline?
A: Commercial travelers to the Coquimbo region typically use La Florida Airport (LSC) in nearby La Serena, which has scheduled service.
transport_tips: Reaching Tambillos Airport generally requires a private vehicle or pre-arranged ground transport, as public transit options to the airfield are limited. Driving from central Coquimbo or La Serena takes approximately 45 minutes to an hour depending on traffic. Rental cars are available more readily in La Serena than directly at the airfield.
local_tip: Carry water and sun protection year-round — the Coquimbo coastal region is known for strong UV exposure and very dry, sunny conditions even in winter, which is useful to remember if you're stepping out of an aircraft on the tarmac.
